sources.title: Learning Quadrupedal Locomotion over Challenging Terrain
sources.specific_reference: Main text Fig. 3D-G and Results pp. 4-5: ten 10 s trials per step height, with success defined as both front and hind legs traversing the step; 0.2 m/s and 0.6 m/s step commands; eight-direction 0.4 m/s flat-ground tracking; average heading error within 10 degrees with and without a 10 kg payload that is 22.7% of total robot mass.

sources.title: Learning robust perceptive locomotion for quadrupedal robots in the wild
sources.specific_reference: Results Fig. 4 and text: ten trials for each fixed-height step from 12 cm to 36.5 cm, successful when overcome within 5 s; a fixed pure-pursuit path over an inclined platform, 20 cm raised platform, stairs 17 cm high by 29 cm deep, and 20 cm block pile; measured 1.2 m/s forward/lateral and 3 rad/s turning commands.

sources.title: Terrain-Aware Quadrupedal Locomotion via Reinforcement Learning
sources.specific_reference: Section IV-A, Fig. 3-5, and Table I: block, stair, stepping-stone, and pole terrains; six commands [0, pi/4, -pi/4, -pi, -5pi/4, -3pi/4], three runs per direction, and maximum travel distance capped at 5 m; stair heights to 15 cm, pole diameters 10-15 cm, and stepping-stone gaps 8.5, 17, and 25.5 cm.

sources.title: Taking the First Step Toward Autonomous Quadruped Robots: The Quadruped Robot Challenge at ICRA 2023 in London
sources.organization: IEEE Robotics & Automation Magazine and NIST
sources.specific_reference: Fig. 2-3 and competition description pp. 155-157: five 7.2 m lanes for small quadrupeds including Unitree Go1, namely 15 degree crossing ramps, 10 cm soft floor with 5 x 10 cm step-overs, 15 cm pallet elevation changes with rolling pipes, 10 x 10 cm K-rails at 45 degrees, and crate terrain with a diagonal negative obstacle; one point is awarded for a run from section start to end without intervention.

sources.title: Barkour: Benchmarking Animal-level Agility with Quadruped Robots
sources.specific_reference: Section III, Table I, Fig. 2, and Appendix B-C: 1 x 1 x 0.1 m pause tables, five weave poles spaced 0.5-0.8 m with 0.1 m torso clearance, a 30 degree 1 m-high A-frame, and a 0.5 x 1 m broad-jump board that must not be touched; full-course score and 10.64 s allotted time; a valid run ends with 5 s standing on the end table.

sources.title: ANYmal - a Highly Mobile and Dynamic Quadrupedal Robot
sources.organization: IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems
sources.specific_reference: Abstract and platform description: the source ANYmal platform is 0.5 m tall. This dimension is used only to make the recorded 0.56 morphology scale conversion to the local Barkour vB package's 0.28 m home base height.

sources.title: MuJoCo Menagerie: Google Barkour vB model
sources.specific_reference: Pinned google_barkour_vb model directory: free-base Barkour vB body, four three-joint legs, twelve direct joint-position general actuators with affine servo bias, joint limits, named foot sites, and base/joint sensors used by the complete local MJCF closure.
